title: ViTrox posts best quarter since listing as volume surges, sees bright outlook
text:
ViTrox posts best quarter since listing as volume surges, sees bright outlook

Friday 06 Nov 2026

KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 5): ViTrox Corporation Bhd (KL: VITROX) is upbeat after the semiconductor equipment maker posted its best quarter since listing in 2005, as higher volume drove down unit costs.

Net profit for the three months ended Sept 30, 2026 (3QFY2026) was RM118.6 million, more than tripled from RM34.7 million a year earlier, according to an exchange filing. Revenue was up more than 110% year-on-year to RM485.1 million.

Looking ahead, ViTrox expects a favourable business environment for the remainder of the financial year and into 2027, supported by robust growth in the semiconductor sector, continued investment in data centre infrastructure and rising demand for edge artificial intelligence (AI) devices.

The company — which makes machines used to automatically inspect and detect defects in semiconductor components and printed circuit board assemblies — said it is seeking to capture a slice of the increasing complexity of AI accelerators and high bandwidth memory.

Net profit in the first nine months of the year also jumped to RM254.8 million from RM87 million a year earlier, supported by sustained capital expenditure deployment from strong AI infrastructure demand and electronics manufacturing customers.

Revenue for the period also more than doubled to RM1.13 billion from RM552.7 million.

“The group will continue to exercise prudent cost management and operational discipline to mitigate potential risks from foreign exchange volatility and geopolitical uncertainties,” ViTrox said.

No interim dividend was declared for the quarter under review, though the company had paid out 1.18 sen per share in July.

Shares of ViTrox ended Thursday at RM10.60, down 30 sen or 2.8%, giving the Penang-based company a market capitalisation of RM20 billion ahead of the results announcement. 

Edited By Jason Ng

title: ViTrox’s 3Q26 profit more than triples | The Star
author: The Star Online
text:
ViTrox’s 3Q26 profit more than triples | The Star

# ViTrox’s 3Q26 profit more than triples 

 Friday, 06 Nov 2026 

Revenue for the third quarter was also higher at RM485.10mil, compared with RM228.57mil a year earlier.

PETALING JAYA: Vitrox Corp Bhd’s profit has more than tripled in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (3Q26), coming in at RM118.58mil compared to RM34.72mil registered in the same quarter last year.

Revenue for the quarter under review was also higher at RM485.10mil, compared with RM228.57mil a year earlier.

In a statement to Bursa Malaysia, the industrial Internet-of-Things solutions provider said the increases were on the back of strong demand across its Automated Board Inspection and Machine Vision System segments.

Both segments were supported by expanded adoption of advanced inspection solutions for artificial intelligence infrastructure and networking equipment.

The group noted that tax incentives from its key subsidiary, ViTrox Technologies Sdn Bhd, contributed to its bottom line.

“We will continue to exercise prudent cost management and operational discipline,” it added.

title: ViTrox Corp - Record Earnings, But Uninviting Risk-Rewards | I3investor
text:
ViTrox Corp - Record Earnings, But Uninviting Risk-Rewards | I3investor

### ViTrox Corp - Record Earnings, But Uninviting Risk-Rewards 

 Date: 2026-11-06 

Firm: RHB Stock: VITROX Price Target: 11.60 Price Call: HOLD Last Price: 9.93 Upside/Downside: +1.67 (16.82%)

- Keep NEUTRAL, new MYR11.60 TP from MYR10.80, 10% upside. ViTrox Corp's 9M26 results was a beat, with yet another record quarterly earnings driven by robust AI-related demand and broad-based growth across its core businesses. We expect earnings to remain supported by a robust orderbook, favourable product mix, and progressive capacity expansion. At above peers' valuation, the slower growth potential - given the high base effect coupled with higher risk premium from the global AI outlook - leaves behind a balanced risk-reward profile.
- Above expectations. 9M26 core earnings rose >2x to MYR253m, above our and consensus' estimates at 81% and 80%. This was driven by stronger revenue growth and margins expansion from improved operating leverage and a favourable product mix, alongside a lower effective tax rate. The stronger operating leverage lifted PBT margins to 26.5% (9M25: 20.9%). Meanwhile, the effective tax rate declined to 15.1% (9M25: 25.7%), benefiting from ViTrox Technologies' (VTSB) tax incentives, lifting earnings margins to 22.6% (9M25: 25.7%).
- Sequential net profit growth continues. 3Q26 revenue rose 29.4% QoQ to MYR485.1m, driven by stronger shipment fulfilment across the automated board inspection (ABI) and machine vision system (MVS) segments, supported by sustained demand for AI infrastructure and networking equipment. The stronger topline, coupled with operating leverage and favourable product mix, lifted PBT by 36.8% QoQ to MYR137m, with PBT margin expanding 1.5ppts to 28.2%. Consequently, core profit increased 56.8% QoQ to MYR118m (2Q26: MYR75m), further supported by a lower effective tax rate of 13.7% (2Q26: 15.5%).
- Positive outlook. We expect earnings momentum to remain robust into FY27, underpinned by sustained AI-related demand and a healthy order pipeline, with incoming orders continuing to outpace shipment capacity. Planned capacity additions should progressively unlock the order backlog from 4Q26 onwards, accelerating shipment conversion and easing the record high book-to-bill ratio. Campus 5.0 (completion targeted by FY28) should drive another step-up in capacity, while renewed pioneer tax incentives provide further earnings tailwinds from FY27 onwards, in our view.
- Earnings and TP. We raise our FY26F-28F earnings by 14%, 8%, and 7% to reflect stronger-than-expected order conversions as shipment volumes ramp up. We expect a favourable product mix, operating leverage, and continued pioneer tax incentives to support earnings growth into FY27. We raise our TP to MYR11.60, pegged to an unchanged 50x (+1.5SD) FY27F P/E. At 46x FY27F P/E, ViTrox's valuation already factors in substantial earnings growth, leaving limited headroom for further re-rating given the slower growth and higher risk premium outlook. Key risks: A slowdown in AI/hyperscaler capex or a broader semiconduction down-cycle, component shortages and capex delays, and margins pressure from Chinese competition and FX. The opposite represents the upside risks.

Source: RHB Research - 6 Nov 2026

title: ViTrox's RM89mil R&D investment delivers 20 new products as revenue hits RM1bil on trailing 12-month basis | Digital News Asia
text:
ViTrox's RM89mil R&D investment delivers 20 new products as revenue hits RM1bil on trailing 12-month basis | Digital News Asia

# ViTrox's RM89mil R&D investment delivers 20 new products as revenue hits RM1bil on trailing 12-month basis

 By Digital News Asia October 22, 2026 

- New products contributed 22.8% of FY2025 revenue as 2026 R&D budget to hit record US$24.49 mil (RM100mil)
- Highlights how sustained investment in Malaysian-developed technology can translate into commercial returns

Penang-based semiconductor inspection equipment maker ViTrox Corporation Bhd generated 22.8% of its FY2025 revenue from new product introductions, offering a measurable indication of how its long-standing investment in research and development (R&D) is translating into commercial success, while offering itself as a role model for its peers in Malaysia.

The contribution was equivalent to approximately US$47.02 million (RM192 million) of the group's US$206.50 million (RM843.1 million) revenue for the year, according to its 2025 Sustainability Report. (pg 95 of the report)

ViTrox introduced 20 new products during the year, double its internal target of 10, while R&D expenditure increased 62.8% to RM89.2 million from RM54.8 million in FY2024.

[RM1 = US$0.245]

The investment represented 10.6% of group revenue, compared with 9.9% a year earlier. (pg 96 of the report)

Building on this success, Virtox expects to allocate more than RM100 million to R&D in 2026, reflecting continued demand for increasingly sophisticated inspection technology.

Beyond company level, these figures provide a useful perspective on Malaysia's ambition to develop more homegrown semiconductor champions under the National Semiconductor Strategy (NSS), launched in May 2024.

Rather than relying exclusively on manufacturing scale, ViTrox has demonstrated an ability to commercialise technology developed through sustained investment in engineering and intellectual property.

Turning research into revenue

ViTrox develops automated optical inspection, three-dimensional inspection and X-ray inspection systems used in semiconductor and electronics manufacturing.

Its technologies serve industries including automotive, telecommunications, computing and aerospace, with increasingly complex semiconductor packaging and artificial intelligence (AI) applications creating additional demand.

The company reported 40 active patents at the end of 2025, reflecting its investment in proprietary technologies.

More importantly, its new product introductions accounted for more than one-fifth of annual revenue, exceeding management's target of 20%.

While the company has not separately disclosed how much of that revenue came specifically from products launched during 2025, the contribution illustrates the commercial importance of its broader innovation pipeline.

In a recent interview with The Edge, co-founder and group CEO Chu Jenn Weng explained that its R&D priorities are shaped partly by its relationships with leading semiconductor manufacturers, cloud service providers and other technology customers.

These relationships provide early visibility into future manufacturing requirements, allowing the company to develop inspection systems ahead of emerging demand.

He also stressed the point that this strategy was built over 15 to 20 years, rather than emerging from any government initiative.

He also identified new product development and customer acquisition as two of ViTrox's most important annual performance indicators.

Revenue milestone strengthens the case

ViTrox's financial performance suggests that its technology investments are contributing to renewed growth.

Revenue increased from RM552.3 million in FY2024 to RM843.1 million in FY2025.

For the first six months of 2026, revenue reached RM642 million, while net profit climbed to RM136.2 million, exceeding the group's full-year 2025 earnings.

On a trailing 12-month basis, revenue reached approximately RM1.16 billion at June 2026, exceeding the RM1 billion annual revenue threshold associated with one of NSS's national-champion ambitions.

What NSS can learn

ViTrox's achievements are particularly relevant to NSS because they demonstrate the importance of sustained, locally developed technological capabilities.

Its proprietary inspection technologies, international customer relationships and R&D strategy were established well before NSS was introduced.

The company has also benefited from government investment incentives and talent-development initiatives, although the available disclosures do not establish that NSS directly caused its recent revenue growth or product-development successes.

That distinction should not diminish its relevance to Malaysia's semiconductor ambitions.

title: ViTrox Gets BUY and MYR12.80 Target Price as AI Demand Builds – Minichart
text:
ViTrox Gets BUY and MYR12.80 Target Price as AI Demand Builds – Minichart

# ViTrox Gets BUY and MYR12.80 Target Price as AI Demand Builds

Posted on October 27, 2026 at 10:43 am (GMT+8)

 

Maybank Investment Bank Berhad (Maybank IBG) — Report dated October 27, 2026

Excerpt from Maybank IBG report.

## Report Summary

### ViTrox Corp (VITRO MK) — Maintain BUY, Target Price Raised to MYR12.80

Maybank IBG has maintained its BUY call on ViTrox Corp, Malaysia’s Shariah-compliant semiconductor vision inspection equipment maker, and lifted its 12-month target price to MYR12.80 from MYR10.50, implying roughly +20% upside from the last quoted share price of MYR10.72. The new TP is based on an unchanged 48x FY27E P/E, the stock’s 5-year forward mean. ViTrox is also retained as the broker’s large cap semiconductor top pick.

- Action: BUY — Target Price MYR12.80 (previously MYR10.50); upside of about 20%.
- Earnings upgrades: FY26E–FY28E core net profit forecasts raised by 32–51% to MYR373m, MYR505m and MYR616m respectively, driven by stronger order deliveries, a favourable tax rate (about 6% effective tax rate in FY27E) and incoming capacity additions.
- Above consensus: Revised forecasts are 19–37% higher than consensus net profit of MYR323m (FY26E), MYR409m (FY27E) and MYR433m (FY28E).
- Key investment idea — demand multi-wave: Current demand is led by US hyperscalers, AI servers and chips to OSAT and EMS players. Maybank IBG expects the next wave from China as HBM capability matures and AI data centre build-out accelerates, reinforced by humanoid robotics and AI inferencing demand.
- Order book signal: The book-to-bill ratio stood at 1.5x in 2Q26 and is expected to stay comfortably above 1x as capacity unlocks. Management’s 7–17% QoQ revenue growth guidance across ABI and MVS is viewed as conservative.
- Capacity expansion in full swing: Campus 2 and 3 are running at >90% utilisation. New warehouses are being built to free up floor space, China operations are targeted for mass production by 1H27, and a new 500k sq ft facility is on track for completion by 2028 to support the next growth leg.
- Key risks: Rising costs, a stronger MYR against the USD, and intensifying competition from China.

Above is an excerpt from a report by Maybank IBG. Clients of Maybank IBG can access the full research report from the Maybank IBG research website.
